content.title: About
content.content: Cooked calamari is a seafood product obtained after a short heat treatment of the body of cephalopod mollusks. It has a delicate, slightly sweet flavor and a tender yet firm texture. Calamari is commonly used in salads, appetizers, pastas, and rice dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Calamari belong to the class Cephalopoda and are relatives of octopuses and cuttlefish.
Calamari flesh is composed of about 80 % water.
They can change skin colour thanks to pigment cells called chromatophores.
In Japan, cooked calamari is often served with soy sauce and wasabi.
There are more than 300 species of calamari, but only a few are widely used in cuisine.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Calamari provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many seafoods, cooked calamari contains little fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports red blood cell formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Calamari is a good source of selenium, zinc and copper, important for immunity and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids and vitamin A in calamari help maintain good vision.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to calamari, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Calamari is rich in purines, so people with gout should limit consumption.

items.title: Contamination risk
items.content: Marine products can contain heavy metals and toxins; purchase from reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked calamari can be sliced into rings or strips and added to salads, pasta, rice rolls, or served as an appetizer with lemon juice and olive oil. It also works well in hot dishes where it quickly reheats without losing tenderness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked calamari in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze it in a sealed bag, where it keeps quality for up to 3 months. Before use, check for off‑odors – a sour or rancid smell indicates spoilage.
